source_text: Sed quaero, cum quibus poetis in talem incurreris Ippocrenem, ut bimembrem bestiam fingeres non quidem carminando, sed blasphemando, cuius corpus de mala necessitate formares et solam faciem nomine libertatis obduceres.
pass_a_gloss: But I ask with which poets you have run into such a Hippocrene, that you would fashion a two-membered beast not indeed by versifying but by blaspheming, whose body you would form from an evil necessity and would overlay only the face with the name of liberty.

lemmas.lexica: LS necessitas; Blaise vs free choice
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: Instead I ask: with which poets did you stumble upon a Hippocrene like this, to invent a two-part beast—not by composing poetry but by blaspheming—whose body you fashioned from an evil necessity while coating only its face with the name of freedom?

choices.why: Loaded word in Julian's Latin at this locus; English follows LS/Blaise range without copying NPNF.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
